prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN)  -- Coalition forces found 26 bodies buried in mass graves and a bloodstained "torture complex," with chains hanging from walls and ceilings and a bed connected to an electrical system, the military said Wednesday. Twenty-six bodies were found in mass graves near a "torture complex" discovered by coalition forces. The troops made the discovery while conducting an operation north of Muqdadiya, Iraq. From December 8 to 11, the troops who found the complex also killed 24 people they said were terrorists and detained 37 suspects, according to a statement issued by Multinational Division North at Camp Speicher in Tikrit. The moves were part of an operation called Iron Reaper that has been in progress across northern Iraq for the past few weeks. The complex was in an area thought to be an al Qaeda in Iraq haven and operating base, the military said. Iraqis had told the military about the site during an earlier operation. "Evidence of murder, torture and intimidation against local villagers was found throughout the area," the military statement said. Ground forces first found what appeared to be a detention facility, which was one of three connected to the torture complex, Multinational Division North said. One of the facilities appeared to have been a headquarters building and a torture facility, it added. As the area was cleared, the bodies were found. Eventually, 26 bodies were uncovered in mass graves next to what were thought to be execution sites, the military said. The bodies are believed to have been dead between six and eight months, according to a gruesome military video shot at the scene. Some had their hands tied behind their backs. Identification is proving to be a challenge because of advanced decomposition. Photos given to the news media show a filthy bed wired to an electrical system, with an outlet hanging from wires on the wall. In the video, troops point out rubber hoses and boxing gloves, a ski mask and a blood-covered sword and knives. Other still photos show an entrance to the underground bunker and barbed wire stretched outside it. A short distance away from the complex, troops found a bullet-riddled Iraqi police vehicle. Some of the bodies may belong to Iraqi police, according to the military video. The operation netted nine weapons caches, which have been destroyed, the military said. They included anti-aircraft weapons, sniper rifles, more than 65 machine guns and pistols, 50 grenades and a surface-to-air missile launcher and platform, the statement said. Also found were mines, pipe bombs, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar tubes and rounds and 130 pounds of homemade explosives. E-mail to a friend .

outputs.L1:
BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN) — Coalition forces discovered 26 bodies buried in mass graves near a bloodstained “torture complex,” where chains hung from walls and ceilings and a bed was wired to an electrical system, the military said Wednesday.

The site was found during an operation north of Muqdadiya, Iraq. From December 8 to 11, the troops who discovered the complex also killed 24 people they identified as terrorists and detained 37 suspects, according to a statement issued by Multinational Division North at Camp Speicher in Tikrit.

The actions were part of Operation Iron Reaper, which has been under way across northern Iraq for the past several weeks. The complex was located in an area the military said was believed to be an al Qaeda in Iraq haven and operating base. Iraqi civilians had alerted the military to the site during an earlier operation.

“Evidence of murder, torture and intimidation against local villagers was found throughout the area,” the military statement said.

Ground forces initially discovered what appeared to be a detention facility, one of three sites connected to the torture complex, Multinational Division North said. One of the facilities appeared to have served as both a headquarters building and a torture site, it added.

As troops cleared the area, they uncovered bodies. In all, 26 bodies were found in mass graves next to what were believed to be execution sites, the military said. According to a graphic military video filmed at the scene, the victims are believed to have been dead for six to eight months. Some had their hands tied behind their backs. Identification has been difficult because of advanced decomposition.

Photographs provided to the news media show a filthy bed wired to an electrical system, with an outlet dangling from wires on the wall. In the video, troops point out rubber hoses and boxing gloves, a ski mask, and a blood-covered sword and knives. Other still images show the entrance to an underground bunker and barbed wire stretched outside it.

A short distance from the complex, troops found a bullet-riddled Iraqi police vehicle. Some of the bodies may be those of Iraqi police officers, according to the military video.

The operation also yielded nine weapons caches, all of which have been destroyed, the military said. The caches included anti-aircraft weapons, sniper rifles, more than 65 machine guns and pistols, 50 grenades, and a surface-to-air missile launcher and platform, according to the statement.

Troops also found mines, pipe bombs, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar tubes and rounds, and 130 pounds of homemade explosives.
outputs.L2:
BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN) — The U.S.-led military coalition said Wednesday that its forces discovered 26 bodies in mass graves, along with a blood-spattered “torture complex” containing chains suspended from walls and ceilings and a bed wired into an electrical system.

The graves were located near the torture site during a coalition operation north of Muqdadiya, Iraq. According to a statement from Multinational Division North at Camp Speicher in Tikrit, the troops who uncovered the complex also killed 24 people they identified as terrorists and arrested 37 suspected individuals between December 8 and 11.

The activity was part of Iron Reaper, an operation that had been underway for several weeks across northern Iraq. The military said the compound was in a region believed to serve as a sanctuary and operational hub for al Qaeda in Iraq. Iraqi civilians had previously alerted forces to the location during an earlier mission.

The military statement said that evidence of killings, torture, and intimidation aimed at nearby villagers was found throughout the site.

Ground troops initially came upon what looked like a detention center, one of three facilities linked to the torture compound, Multinational Division North said. Another structure appeared to function both as a headquarters and as a torture site. As soldiers secured and searched the area, they began finding bodies. In all, 26 bodies were recovered from mass graves beside areas believed to have been used for executions, the military said.

A graphic military video recorded at the scene indicated that the victims were thought to have been dead for six to eight months. Some were found with their hands bound behind their backs. Because the bodies were badly decomposed, identifying them has been difficult.

Photographs released to news organizations showed a dirty bed connected to electrical wiring, with an outlet dangling from wires on a wall. In the video, soldiers pointed to rubber hoses, boxing gloves, a ski mask, and knives and a sword covered in blood. Other images showed the entrance to an underground bunker, with barbed wire stretched outside.

Not far from the complex, troops also discovered an Iraqi police vehicle riddled with bullet holes. The military video said some of the recovered bodies may have been Iraqi police officers.

The military said the operation also uncovered nine weapons caches, all of which were destroyed. The stockpiles included anti-aircraft weapons, sniper rifles, more than 65 machine guns and pistols, 50 grenades, and a surface-to-air missile launcher with its platform. Forces also found mines, pipe bombs, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar tubes and rounds, and 130 pounds of homemade explosives.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a CNN-style news article about coalition forces discovering mass graves and a torture complex near Muqdadiya, Iraq, including details from Operation Iron Reaper and weapons caches found.
counterfactuals.output:
**Coalition forces uncover mass graves, alleged torture site near Muqdadiya**

**MUQDADIYA, Iraq** — Coalition and Iraqi security forces conducting operations in Diyala province discovered several mass graves and what officials described as a torture complex near the city of Muqdadiya, the U.S. military said, as troops continued a major offensive aimed at disrupting insurgent networks northeast of Baghdad.

The discoveries were made during **Operation Iron Reaper**, a coalition campaign targeting al Qaeda in Iraq and affiliated extremist groups operating in Diyala and other volatile areas. Military officials said the operation was intended to deny insurgents safe havens, clear weapons caches and restore security in communities that had suffered from sectarian violence and militant intimidation.

According to coalition statements, patrols near Muqdadiya found multiple burial sites containing the remains of people believed to have been killed by insurgents. Nearby, troops also located a facility described by military officials as a torture complex, containing rooms and equipment allegedly used to detain and abuse captives.

Officials said the findings underscored the brutality of extremist groups that had entrenched themselves in parts of Diyala province, where residents had reported kidnappings, killings and threats against those who cooperated with Iraqi authorities or coalition forces.

During the same series of operations, coalition forces reported uncovering multiple **weapons caches** in the area. The seized materiel included rifles, machine guns, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar rounds, artillery shells, explosives and components used to build improvised explosive devices, or IEDs. Troops also found ammunition, bomb-making materials and other military equipment hidden in rural areas and abandoned structures, officials said.

Military commanders said the caches appeared intended to support attacks on Iraqi civilians, Iraqi security forces and coalition patrols. The seizure of explosives and munitions was described as a key part of the broader effort to reduce roadside bomb attacks in Diyala, one of Iraq’s most contested provinces at the time.

Operation Iron Reaper followed a series of offensives designed to pressure insurgent groups that had moved out of Baghdad and into surrounding provinces. Diyala, with its mixed Sunni and Shiite population and difficult terrain of farmland, palm groves and villages, had become a major battleground as militants sought to exploit sectarian tensions and weak local security.

Coalition officials said Iraqi forces played a role in the searches and clearing operations, while local residents provided information that helped lead troops to suspected insurgent sites. Commanders said cooperation from civilians was critical to locating hidden graves, detention sites and weapons stockpiles.

The discoveries near Muqdadiya added to growing evidence of the toll of insurgent violence in the province. Military officials said the remains found in the graves would be handled by Iraqi authorities, who would work to identify victims and investigate the killings.

No immediate casualty figures from the graves were independently confirmed, and officials did not release the identities of the victims. The U.S. military said operations in the area would continue as Iraqi and coalition forces searched for additional caches, safe houses and suspected insurgent leaders.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

**BAGHDAD, Iraq (AP) —** Military authorities said Tuesday that troops uncovered an alleged torture facility during a security operation in Iraq, finding detainees held in harsh conditions alongside chains, electrical devices, suspected execution sites and a cache of weapons.

In a statement released in Baghdad, the military said the site was discovered during a sweep targeting armed groups accused of kidnappings, intimidation and sectarian violence. Officials said soldiers entering the compound found multiple rooms believed to have been used to hold and abuse prisoners, including areas equipped with metal chains and wiring that investigators said may have been used to administer electric shocks.

The statement said several detainees were found inside the facility and were given medical attention before being transferred to Iraqi authorities for identification and interviews. Military officials did not immediately release the number of detainees or provide details about their conditions, citing an ongoing investigation.

Troops also identified what the statement described as apparent execution areas at or near the compound. Investigators were examining those locations for forensic evidence, the military said. It was not immediately clear how long the facility had been operating or how many people may have been held there.

Weapons and military equipment seized during the raid included rifles, ammunition, grenades and other materiel, according to the statement. The military said the cache appeared to be intended for use by insurgent or militia elements operating in the area.

No immediate information was provided on arrests made during the operation. The military said the site had been secured and that evidence collected there would be turned over to the appropriate investigative authorities.

The discovery comes amid continuing concerns over unlawful detention sites and abuses carried out by armed groups in Iraq. Human rights organizations have repeatedly warned that kidnappings, torture and extrajudicial killings have fueled fear in communities already strained by years of violence.

Military officials said the operation was part of a broader effort to dismantle armed networks and protect civilians. The statement did not identify the group believed to have controlled the facility, and officials said additional details would be released as the investigation develops.

**Multinational forces uncover bodies, detention sites and weapons north of Muqdadiya**

**MUQDADIYA, Iraq** — Multinational Division North forces uncovered multiple bodies, suspected detention facilities and weapons caches during a security operation north of Muqdadiya, military officials said.

The operation, conducted in coordination with Iraqi security forces, targeted areas believed to have been used by insurgent groups to detain civilians and stage attacks, officials said. Troops discovered what appeared to be makeshift holding areas, along with evidence suggesting the sites had been used to imprison and intimidate local residents.

During the search, forces also found several bodies. Authorities did not immediately release the number of victims or their identities, saying the remains would be examined and efforts made to notify families.

Weapons and related materials were also recovered during the operation, including small arms, ammunition and other military-style equipment, officials said. The items were secured for further investigation or destruction.

Muqdadiya, located in Diyala province, has long been a contested area where sectarian violence, insurgent activity and criminal networks have overlapped. Military officials said the discoveries underscore the continued threat posed by armed groups operating in rural areas north of the city.

“This operation was aimed at disrupting networks that have terrorized local communities,” a military spokesperson said. “The discovery of detention facilities and bodies shows the brutality these groups are capable of.”

Iraqi authorities are expected to lead follow-up investigations into the detention sites and the recovered remains. Security forces said additional operations may be conducted in the area as they work to identify those responsible and prevent the sites from being used again.

## Coalition Forces Discover 26 Bodies, Suspected Torture Rooms During Operation Iron Reaper in Iraq

Coalition forces conducting Operation Iron Reaper in Iraq discovered 26 decomposed bodies, suspected torture rooms, and multiple weapons caches during a series of searches targeting militant activity, military officials said.

The bodies were found in areas believed to have been used by insurgent groups for detention, interrogation, and executions. Due to the advanced state of decomposition, officials said identification of the victims and determination of the exact causes of death would require further forensic examination.

During the operation, troops also uncovered rooms suspected of being used for torture. The sites reportedly contained evidence consistent with prolonged detention and abuse, though officials did not immediately release detailed descriptions, citing the ongoing investigation and the need to preserve evidence.

In addition to the human remains, coalition forces found weapons caches that included firearms, ammunition, and explosive materials. Military officials said the caches were likely intended to support attacks against Iraqi security forces, coalition personnel, and civilians.

Operation Iron Reaper was launched as part of broader efforts to disrupt insurgent networks, seize weapons, and restore security in areas affected by militant activity. Coalition commanders said the discoveries underscored the brutality of the groups operating in the region and the continuing threat they posed to local communities.

Iraqi authorities were expected to work with coalition investigators to identify the victims and determine whether the sites were linked to specific insurgent factions. Officials said recovered weapons and forensic evidence would be analyzed for intelligence that could lead to further arrests or operations.

The discovery of the bodies and suspected torture facilities has renewed concerns about the scale of abuses committed by armed groups during the conflict. Coalition officials said the operation would continue as forces searched for additional caches, safe houses, and evidence tied to militant networks.
